title: Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 Reveals New Mizu Image Ahead of January Premiere
excerpt:
A fresh preview offers another look at Mizu's return to Netflix.
Season 2 premieres January 19, 2027, with a third and final season also planned.
body_md:
Blue Eye Samurai is moving closer to its long-awaited second season, and a newly shared image provides another glimpse of Mizu in action. The animated drama emerged as a standout Netflix release after its first season, earning Emmy recognition and building an audience eager to follow the next stage of its revenge story. The new preview adds to that anticipation without revealing much about specific scenes.

The second season is scheduled for a worldwide Netflix premiere on January 19, 2027. Its episode count has not yet been announced. Although the promotional image highlights the protagonist's return, it should not be mistaken for a full trailer or a comprehensive explanation of the coming storyline.

Co-creators Amber Noizumi and Michael Green are returning as writers and executive producers. Erwin Stoff is also an executive producer, while Jane Wu serves as supervising director and producer. Animation production remains with Blue Spirit, continuing the studio partnership responsible for the distinctive visual approach of the first season.

The returning voice cast includes Maya Erskine as Mizu, Brenda Song as Akemi, Darren Barnet as Taigen, Masi Oka as Ringo and Kenneth Branagh as Abijah Fowler. Newly announced performers include Jonathan Pryce as Old Violet, Joel Kim Booster as Priest Ando and Sherry Cola as Kuma. Additional returning characters may still be revealed, but their participation has not been confirmed in the available announcement.

The story resumes after Mizu's uneasy arrangement with Fowler at the conclusion of the first season. Having learned that the people she seeks are in London, she must leave Japan and confront a profoundly different society. The creators have previously discussed how the journey will force her to experience being visibly Asian in a predominantly white environment and to encounter the restrictions imposed on women in the period's England.

Netflix's plans extend beyond this next installment. A third season is already in development and has been identified as the final chapter of the series. No release window has been provided for that concluding season. January's return is therefore a major continuation of Mizu's journey rather than the announced end of her story.
